turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Hi there, I'm Dr.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Cuema Sant, one of the dermatologists here. Did you find parking okay?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That garage is a maze. Ha, it really is. I went around twice before I found a spot on level three. Everybody does.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So before we start, can you tell me your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Ashling Brennan, and my birthday is June 9th, 1988.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you, Ashling. Your referral mentions a mole on your back. Tell me what's going on with it. So it's on my left upper back,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: kind of by my shoulder blade. My husband Declan noticed it looked different back in arm July. He says it's gotten bigger and darker since spring.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: has it bled at all,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: or crusted over?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, no bleeding.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does it itch or hurt?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It itches a little now and then, it doesn't hurt.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you ever had a skin cancer yourself, or any moles removed?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I've never had skin cancer, and and nothing's ever been removed.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Anyone in the family with skin cancer.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My dad had a basal cell on his nose a few years ago. They scraped it off and he's been fine. Good to know.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How about sun exposure?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Some burns growing up, tanning beds.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Oh, lots of sun.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I was a lifeguard every summer through college at Crestview Aquatics. I got burned pretty badly a few times like blistering. Never did tanning beds though.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Garded any medicines you take regularly.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Just levothiric sign,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: 75 micrograms every morning for my thyroid. And any allergies to medications,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: or to lidocaine, or latex?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: No allergies that I know of. Alright, let me take a look.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Can you slip your left arm out of the gown?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: So on your left upper back, just over the shoulder blade,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: there's a 7mm dark brown mole.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's asymmetric,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: the border is irregular and kind of nudged at the bottom, and there's a black area on one side. under the dermatoscope I see an irregular network and a few darts at the edge. That one stands out from your other moles.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Is that bad?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It's what we call an ugly duckling. It doesn't look like its neighbours. Let me check the rest of you first. Your back, chest and arms have scattered two to three millimetre round moles evenly brown.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Those all look like normal benign moles. Scalp,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: face and legs look fine. I don't feel any swollen lymph nodes in your left armpit or your neck, and he lumps you've noticed in your armpit.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, so here's what I think. This mole on your back has several changing features. Most of these turn out to be in a typical mole,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: but I can't rule out an early melanoma just by looking, so I'd like to do a biopsy today. Today, okay,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: what does that involve? It's a shave biopsy.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I numb the area with a little lidocaine with epinephrine, then Then I take off the whole mole with a thin blade,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: fairly deep,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: and send it to the lab.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: No stitches.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: You'll have a shallow wound,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: kind of like a scrape.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's fine, let's do it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Great, a little pinch and a burn now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: and that's done, it went well. I've sent it to pathology. For care, keep the bandage on for 24 hours,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: then wash it gently once a day,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: put on plain petroleum jelly and a fresh bandage every day until it heals. That's usually one to two weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, when will I know?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Results take about seven to ten days. They'll post to the portal and someone will call you either way. What's the best number for you?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My cell,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: 555 -0163. And my portal email is AshlingDartBrenon88 at fastmail .com.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Gartid, if it does come back as a melanoma,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: we talk about a wider excision to get clear margins, but let's not get ahead of ourselves. ourselves. If the site gets red,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: hard,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: swollen, or drains pass, call us.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, should I be doing anything about the sun?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Yes, broad spectrum sunscreen, SPF 30 or higher, every day on exposed skin, reapply every two hours when you're outside, and a wide -brimmed hat. Check your own moles once a month, and since you've had blistering sunburns and quite a few moles, I'd like to see you for a full skin check every year. Sounds good. Let's book a follow -up for the biopsy site and results on Tuesday October 27th.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Any other questions?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: No, I think that's it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thank you. You're welcome,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Ashling.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Take care and good luck getting out of that garage.
